note: Cross-implementation conformance vectors for the `rd board`/`rd board --with-key` single-board URL fragment (ready-b78, follow-up to ready-df0/ready-df6). Each vector's `fragment` is the exact string cmd/rd/board.go's ownBoardURL/boardKeyFragment.cekParam produce for the given (coord, relays, viewer, ceks) inputs. cmd/rd/board_fragment_conformance_test.go replays this file through the REAL ownBoardURL against the SAME fixed inputs and asserts byte equality; web/board/src/lib/fragment.conformance.test.ts imports this SAME committed file and asserts the REAL parseFragment (fragment.ts) decodes `fragment` back into `expect`. Neither side re-derives the other's grammar from a hand-typed regex -- a change to either implementation that breaks the other fails here, not silently.

vectors.name: with_key_single_epoch
vectors.note: The ready-df0 shape: board coordinate, one relay, a public viewer pubkey, one held CEK epoch.

vectors.name: with_key_multi_epoch_ascending
vectors.note: A rotated board: TWO held CEK epochs. cekParam sorts ascending by epoch regardless of map iteration order, and every held epoch travels (not just the newest) so older-sealed cards still open.

vectors.name: no_key_relays_only
vectors.note: `rd board --no-key` / `rd board share`: a nil boardKeyFragment must emit the pre-ready-df0 bytes exactly -- no pk=, no cek=.

vectors.name: with_key_two_relays
vectors.note: Multiple relays, comma-joined before percent-encoding -- parseRelays on the TS side must split on the LITERAL comma inside the decoded relays= value, not on an encoded one.
